chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Astarabadi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Yusuf ibn Muhammad narrated to me, from Ziyad, from his father, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn Musa al-Rida, from his father Musa ibn Ja'far, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them).

He said: When Gabriel brought the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) the news of the death of al-Najashi, he cried a sad cry for him and said: 'Your brother Sahman, who is the name of al-Najashi, has died.' Then he went out to the graveyard and prayed over him, saying Allahu Akbar seven times. So God lowered every elevated place for him until he saw his corpse while he was in Ethiopia.

key_terms.النِّجَاشِيِّ: Title for the Christian king of Abyssinia (Ethiopia)
key_terms.كَبَّرَ سَبْعًا: Said 'Allahu Akbar' seven times (a specific form of funeral prayer)

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad do when he received news of al-Najashi's death?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Khisal highlights the Prophet Muhammad’s (peace be upon him) unique honor of performing Salat al-Gha'ib (funeral prayer for the absent) for the Christian king al-Najashi, a precedent for interfaith respect in Shia tradition. The miraculous lowering of the hills of Ethiopia to allow him to view the corpse underscores the divine confirmation of al-Najashi’s righteousness, distinguishing him from other non-Muslims. This event is often cited by scholars to validate the permissibility of praying over righteous non-Muslims who were allies of the Muslims.
